title: Chris Kelly and his blues playing
summary: Milton left Kelly's band after a couple of jobs; Kelly played blues with a hat or plunger mute.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: Did you ever play with Chris Kelly? I've heard about him. He's another...
I played with Chris Kelly a couple of jobs, I mean. But I left him. I mean, I didn't like his ways. I left him. I didn't stay with him.
How was his style? Was it anything like either Armstrong or like Buddy Batista?
No, no, no, no. He's... He had his own style, him. He had his own style. I've heard he was very good in the blues.

He was good. That's what he was bad on, blues than anything. He was bad on blues than anything. In other words, I believe he was one of the best blues trumpet players that he had. I mean, that's mostly what he used to do, blues mostly.
Did he use a lot of mutes? Chris Kelly?
No, he mostly used his hat, him and his hand, you know what I mean? Well, he's just a youth that are taller than the other one. Yeah, that and flush that.

At that time when he had a bigger band, what you call him used to mostly lead these bands, Ricard. Remember when him and Ricard had a band together? That was before we got stuck playing bass. He used to lead the band.
I knew he played trumpet in the old days. I heard him once in a parade. He's a nice trumpet player.
Yeah, that's what I heard. Nice trumpet player.
Boy, you had a job, brother. That's right.
